canonicalIdScope: local to this installation; the board's Y1/Y2/Y3 are a different, external series and are not reused here

@graph.title: Shipping
@graph.summary: Read the list by what each item would prove, and how soon.

cf:meaning.title: Done means someone outside the work can use it
cf:meaning.excerpt: Not merged, not demoed — used. Until then the task is in progress under a different name.

cf:meaning.title: A task earns its place by what it would prove
cf:meaning.excerpt: The version that answers the open question soonest beats the version that is complete.

cf:meaning.title: Shipping means deployed, not merged
cf:meaning.excerpt: Contested. Merging closes the authoring loop; only deploying closes the user's.

cf:clarification.title: Deploy is a separate gate with its own owner

@graph.title: Commitment
@graph.summary: Read the list as promises made to named people.

cf:meaning.title: A task with no named person is not a commitment
cf:meaning.excerpt: It is an intention. Intentions do not have deadlines and should not be treated as though they do.

cf:meaning.title: A late promise is worse than a withdrawn one
cf:meaning.excerpt: Withdrawing returns the decision to the other person while they can still act on it.

cf:clarification.title: Applies to dates given aloud, not only written ones

@graph.title: Capacity
@graph.summary: Read the list against the hours that actually exist, not the ones on the calendar.

cf:meaning.title: Some work only happens in unbroken stretches
cf:meaning.excerpt: An hour split in three is not an hour for this class of task; it is nothing.

cf:clarification.title: Two hours is the observed floor for the deep class

cf:meaning.title: A list longer than the week is a backlog, not a plan
cf:meaning.excerpt: Calling it a plan makes every item feel late.

@graph.title: Risk
@graph.summary: Read the list by what fails without anyone noticing.

cf:meaning.title: Work is done when its failing is loud
cf:meaning.excerpt: Not when it works. Anything that can fail silently eventually will, and the cost lands far from here.

cf:meaning.title: Reversible decisions deserve speed; irreversible ones deserve the time saved
cf:meaning.excerpt: Most of the list is reversible and is being treated as though it is not.

cf:clarification.title: Anything touching customer data is treated as irreversible

cf:meaning.title: An unowned task is an outage waiting for a date
